title: Nested Return in a Composite Diamond Clock: A Welded-Seam Audit of Phase Projection, Thermal Nulling, and Residual-Burden Migration
source_native_claims: Manuscript type (source-stated): Tier-2 domain-closure study / independent secondary analysis.

Two experimentally distinct operations act on different representational spaces: TTZFS-8 eight-phase cycling suppresses pulse-error-generated spectral components (phase-space projection), and a composite D/Q estimator nulls first-order thermal drift while preserving the common oscillator mode (channel-space thermal nulling).
Once the dominant thermal mode is removed, a previously subdominant residual becomes the governing burden (residual-burden migration).

The source (Lourette et al.) does not provide a GCD return contract, seam-accounting profile, return credit, residual tolerance, or RunID; 'welded-seam audit' names the audit burden, not a pre-granted weld, and canonical weld cannot be inferred from local restoration (NON_EVALUABLE absent return/seam contract).

The local operators do not redefine canonical tau_R or the reserved invariants F, omega, S, C, kappa, IC; a separate UMCP run would require its own object definition, adapter, bounded trace, missingness policy, return domain, metric, tolerance, closure registry, and run identity.
